engineering-fundamentals.md: Build a shared vocabulary for performance, state, coordination and failure. Follow thirteen chapters from the cost of a loop to the boundaries that keep an overloaded system usable.
engineering-fundamentals/complexity-anal: Count growing work, expose hidden boundary costs, and separate asymptotic bounds from measured UI deadlines.
engineering-fundamentals/latency-vs-thro: Measure request time and completion rate separately, then reason about queueing, tails and saturation.
engineering-fundamentals/sync-vs-async.m: Track completion, thread occupancy and task lifetime without assuming that suspend means non-blocking.
engineering-fundamentals/coupling-vs-coh: Design boundaries around changes, dependency contracts and the work that belongs together.
engineering-fundamentals/immutability.md: Follow references, published versions and update observation to build state readers can trust.
engineering-fundamentals/caching.md: Make cache freshness, stale-fill races and miss-path capacity explicit before trading memory for speed.
engineering-fundamentals/backpressure.md: Trace bounded demand, queued items and overload choices from a slow consumer back to its producer.
engineering-fundamentals/time-and-clocks: Choose a clock for elapsed time, calendar time or causality, and test the assumptions that distinguish them.
engineering-fundamentals/fault-tolerance: Contain a failed dependency while preserving correctness, bounded work and a measurable recovery contract.
Make valid modes, transition rules and recoverable effects explicit.
engineering-fundamentals/queues.md: Separate admission, processing and acknowledgement without hiding overload.
engineering-fundamentals/event-driven-ar: Choose event, command and state contracts that consumers can recover from.
engineering-fundamentals/serialization.m: Carry data across boundaries without losing schema or compatibility guarantees.
